::: {.letter-metadata}
**Date:** Sept 19th [1885]  
**From:** Elderfield  
**Manuscript:** MS Princeton University, Parrish Collection
:::

My dear [Miss Gordon Cumming](people/person_571.qmd)

Thank you so very much for the photos, I am very glad to have it. I am afraid this is no return, as it was taken from a not very good picture. [Bassano’](people/person_2361.qmd)s negatives are used up and he has been intreating me to come again- but I have not been in London for two years.[^1] If ever we are there at the same time, I do hope we may get beyond photographs.

Yes, I look at the [Mungoose](other_books/otherbook_990.qmd) & consider of him, but I am afraid I must finish off other things before Christmas which have got into type by a sort of mistake for the Christmas number.[^2] I had a scolding about it from the publisher and must appease him.

Yours sincerely
C M Yonge

---

[^1]: Alexander Bassano (1829-1913), a London photographer.
[^2]: C. F. Gordon Cumming, ‘The Rabbit Plague in Australasia’ *MP* 3s 12 (July 1886), 58-69, discusses the possibility that the introduction of the mongoose might control the rabbits.
